title: One Quarter of Americans Embarrassed by Coffee Order
paragraphs: Would you like some peanuts with your coffee? How about in it — with some maple syrup?
That was one of the unusual recipes shared in a recent Talker Research survey of around 1,600 US coffee drinkers.
As well as finding out about some unusual coffee orders, the survey found that people have strong opinions about what belongs in a cup.
One in three said they judge others by their coffee preferences. And 23% had orders they only get in secret because they worry about being judged themselves.
For example, one person mixed coffee with black tea. Another said they preferred a double espresso with five sugars, a teaspoon of butter, whipped cream and caramel syrup.
Other extras included marshmallows, cinnamon, salt and honey.
Only 14% of respondents preferred their coffee black, without anything added.
As for the coffee itself, 58% preferred a medium roast, while 21% preferred a light roast and another 21% preferred a dark roast.
Participants were also asked which drinks they thought counted as coffee.
Pumpkin spice lattes passed the test for 67%, while 78% accepted Frappuccinos, the iced drinks sold by Starbucks. However, 56% counted chai — a type of tea — as coffee, too!
So if someone judges your coffee order, ask them about theirs — you might find that theirs is weirder than yours!
